bullets.text: Clear definitions help distinguish meaningful practices amid rapid change, shallow reactions, and AI hype.
IDE integration made AI assistance more contextual and encouraged programmers to trust generated code.
Karpathy's definition emphasizes accepting changes and chasing outcomes without closely inspecting the underlying implementation.
Natural-language app builders offer immediate gratification, but broad requests can unravel without technical understanding.
Dietschy's eventual success illustrates the persistence and frustration that unguided iteration can demand.
The human must curate relevant context as work moves between broad goals and small implementation tasks.
Requirements, architecture, task breakdowns, and success criteria prepare agents to pursue defined outcomes with less supervision.

sections.label: Judge the method behind the demo

bullets.text: Early guidelines can preserve easy app creation while supporting more reliable changes and small-team execution.
The author assesses technical ability through daily building practices, not the apparent completeness of a prototype.
The essay proposes that prototype excitement can conceal the integration, architecture, and security work needed for production.
Reported weak enterprise returns frame a warning against experiments disconnected from measurable business value.
The author still vibe codes, but only after establishing the context that makes delegation effective.
Fast prototypes can test ideas; building something real requires discipline beyond the initial creative rush.

notes.text: The definition turns on what the human stops doing: reading diffs and inspecting structure. Merely typing natural language does not capture the behavioral distinction the author is trying to preserve.
Dietschy's eventual success matters: the objection is not that a prototype can never work, but that unguided iteration burns effort and offers little control as scope grows.
When the agent judges itself against predefined success criteria, how will you test whether those criteria capture the real requirement rather than merely reward a passing result?

The pilot-failure explanation is explicitly a hypothesis. The cited return figures supply context for the concern; they do not, within this essay, establish vibe coding as the cause of those failures.
The ending keeps vibe coding as useful experimentation rather than forbidding it. The boundary is whether a convincing demonstration is being mistaken for a system ready to ship.
